question_type: geometric mean over 80 monthly cells of one panel (Budget expenditures) of a three-panel months-by-calendar-year table (Table 6, Summary by Months and Calendar Years); vintage pinned by the question's own scope ('just the calendar years 1940-1949'); several cells are OCR misreads that make their rows fail the printed row total
decisive_step: Two coupled decisions. (1) Extraction: on the rows whose cells do not sum to the printed Total (show_table's 'identity FAILS' rows), treat the offending cell as an OCR misread and repair it from the other printings of the same table (majority) and the row total; the reference did this in worklog.md Step 5 (extract_all.py: per-row total check plus per-cell majority over the 12 in-range printings) and confirmed with the receipts-minus-surplus identity in calc.py. (2) Vintage: use only the printings whose Table 6 rows span exactly 1940-1949 (Mar 1949 .. Feb 1950 issues) and reject Mar 1950 onward, which widen the year span and re-base the 1948 months for the Foreign Economic Cooperation Trust Fund; worklog.md Step 3 and solution.json decisions[0]. Because every in-range printing carries the same repaired values (worklog Step 5, last bullet), (1) is what separated a from c and from b2's first submit; (2) is what the gate broke for b and b2.

a.path_summary: find_tables restricted to --years 1940-1949 (a[5]) led to Table 6 in the Dec 1949 issue (a[8], a[10]) with the 'identity FAILS at lines 364,374,376,394' note on screen. It compared the expenditure rows with the Nov 1949 printing (a[19]-[22]), used calc row sums against the printed totals to identify the July 1943 misread (a[25]-[28]) and the Jan 1945 misread (a[29]-[32], a[45]), checked the 1948 cells that differed between Nov and Dec with printings and kept the latest (a[40]-[44], they were revisions, not OCR), computed the 80-value geometric mean (a[38]), computed the raw-cells alternative (a[48]) and rejected it after estimating each cell's effect on the mean (a[49], a[55]).

tool_use.friction: printings' SUMMARY 'latest printing' line pointed at another panel's row of the same year (surplus/deficit) because the tool keys cells by period+column only: a[13], a[24], a[32]. printings --row 'Budget expenditures' found nothing because --row is a period (a[14]-[16], had to read --help). show_table --from-row combined with --grep returned no rows (a[50]-[51]). find_tables --years 1940-1949 hid every 1950+ issue, which is the accidental reason a never faced the re-based 1951 vintage. ~25 of 56 steps went to the cell repair.

a.text_use: acted on 'If a value you use sits on such a row, compare it with another printing' (quoted at a[28] and a[45]) and on 'use the latest printing of each value' for the 1948 revisions (a[40]-[44]); a[45] notes the sentence does not say what to do after comparing ('doesn't explicitly say choose majority')

b.path_summary: find_tables --all (b[6]) then --years 1950-1951 (b[9]) took it to the Feb 1951 and Feb 1950 printings. show_table 1951_02 --stitch (b[11], b[13]) misaligned rows across the three panels (noticed at b[23]); show_table 1950_02 (b[16], b[18]) showed the FAILS note for its rows. It read the raw 1951_02 lines via the python reader (b[22]) and understood the FECTF re-basing of 1948 (b[23]). One calc (b[24]) produced two candidates: the raw Feb 1950 cells (two OCR-misread cells kept) and the re-based 1951_02 set. It submitted the Feb 1950 candidate with the other as --alt (b[27]). The gate's later_printing finding offered a substitute for the May 1942 cell whose 'latest printing' was the receipts-panel row of the same year; b saw this (b[28]: 'line 384 in 1951_02 is receipts row, not expenditures') and accepted anyway (b[29]), which moved the answer from ~0.1% low to ~2.6% low.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Used the raw Feb 1950 cells for May 1942 and Nov 1947 although both rows were flagged 'identity FAILS' at b[16]/b[18]; no row-sum or cross-printing check. Its first candidate equals the reference's rejected 'raw Feb 1950 OCR' alternative (solution.json alternatives_considered).
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: The reference summed each row against its printed total, took the per-cell majority over the 12 in-range printings and confirmed with receipts minus surplus (worklog Step 5, calc.py). Cell a did the same by hand on the Dec 1949 printing (a[25]-[34]).

tool_use.friction: --stitch misaligned the three panels' rows (b[12], b[23]); --grep with a line-number regex returned nothing (b[16]-[17]); direct sed on the corpus path was denied (b[20]) so it used the python reader (b[22]); the gate's substitute came from a different panel (b[28]). Only 13 requests: no printings call and no validation before the first submit.

b.harness_use: One gate round. Finding later_printing: 'Your answer uses treasury_bulletin_1950_02.txt:385 (May) ...; latest printing treasury_bulletin_1951_02.txt:384 ... (latest wins unless a date is pinned)' plus an Offer recomputed with that cell. The substitute was the Net budget receipts row of the same year (several times smaller), not an expenditures cell. b noticed the panel mismatch at b[28] and still accepted ('Harness says latest wins ... Need accept per instruction'). The gate changed the answer, from wrong-by-two-OCR-cells to wrong-by-a-wrong-panel-cell. No loop notes, no compaction, no ledger splice. The pilot-1 analysis notes that competing_candidates and flagged_cells also matched but only later_printing was shown.

b2.path_summary: find_tables --years 1940-1949 (b2[6]) led to Table 6 in Dec 1949; show_table --long (b2[9], b2[11]) showed the FAILS note; it printed the raw lines (b2[14]) and ran printings on one cell, whose summary pointed at the surplus panel (b2[16]-[17]). It computed the 80-value geometric mean from the raw Dec 1949 cells, including the July 1943 and Jan 1945 misreads (b2[19]), and submitted (b2[21]); that value is the same one c answered. The gate's later_printing finding said the Mar 1942 cell's latest printing was 1951_02:384 (again the receipts-panel row) and offered a recomputation. b2 neither accepted nor kept: it read 'latest wins' as an instruction to re-source all 80 cells from the Feb 1951 printing (b2[22]-[30]), saw that 1948 June onward differ (b2[31], the FECTF re-basing) and that several 1943/1945 cells differ (a mix of the Dec 1949 misreads being absent and new 1951 misreads), recomputed (b2[32]) and submitted (b2[34]); wrong by under 1%.

first_divergence.what_it_did: Kept the raw cells of the two identity-FAILS rows (July 1943, Jan 1945) with no comparison against another printing, although the FAILS note was on screen at b2[11] and its AGENTS.md carried the compare-another-printing sentence. Secondary divergence after the gate: SOURCE_ISSUE_VINTAGE at b2[22]-[32], moving to the Feb 1951 printing whose table spans 1932-1950 and carries the re-based 1948 months.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: Cell a compared the flagged rows with the Nov 1949 printing and used row sums vs printed totals to pick the uncorrupted digits (a[25]-[34], a[45]); the reference used row totals plus a 12-printing majority (worklog Step 5) and stayed on the printings whose rows are exactly 1940-1949 (worklog Step 3).

tool_use.friction: printings summary 'latest' line pointed at the surplus panel (b2[17]); find_tables --years 1940-1949 hid the 1950-51 issues so the gate's reference to 1951_02 came as a surprise (b2[22]); show_table 1951_02 --long --grep 1942 showed only the first panel's row (b2[26]-[29]) so it fell back to sed on raw lines (b2[28], b2[30]); 80 values hand-typed twice (b2[19], b2[32]).

b2.text_use: 'use the latest printing of each value' was followed (b2[15], and decisively at b2[22]: 'Need use latest printings for all cells'); 'If a value you use sits on such a row, compare it with another printing' was ignored at b2[19]; 'Compute every final number with calc' followed
b2.harness_use: One gate round, 2 submits. Finding later_printing on the Mar 1942 expenditures cell (1949_12:373) naming 1951_02:384 as the latest printing with an Offer (a slightly different value). The named line is the receipts-panel row of 1942 in 1951_02, not an expenditures cell. b2 did not run either the Accept or the Keep line; it treated 'latest wins unless a date is pinned' as a rule and rebuilt the whole series from the 1951 printing. The gate therefore changed the answer from one wrong value (raw in-range cells) to a different wrong value (re-based vintage); had b2 kept its first answer it would still have been wrong, like c. Of the 5 remaining rules (answer_count, later_printing, period_match, recompute_final, scale) only later_printing fired. No loop notes, no compaction.

c.path_summary: Two find_tables calls (c[5], c[7]) led to Table 6 in Dec 1949; three show_table pages (c[10], c[12], c[14]) with the FAILS note on screen at c[10] and c[12]. One printings call whose summary pointed at the surplus panel (c[16]-[17]). Its first calc had 78 values (c[19]); it re-listed to 80 (c[21]) and answered the raw Dec 1949 cells including the July 1943 and Jan 1945 misreads (c[23]), off by under 0.1%. Its answer equals b2's first submit and the raw-cells alternative that a computed and rejected at a[48].

first_divergence.what_it_did: Took the raw cells of the two identity-FAILS rows without opening a second printing or summing the rows; the only doubt it voiced was about the panel and the vintage (c[17], c[22]), never the cell digits.
first_divergence.what_a_right_cell_or_the_reference_did: Cell a treated the FAILS note as a trigger, compared with the Nov 1949 printing and repaired both cells from the row totals (a[19]-[34]); the reference did the same with a 12-printing majority (worklog Step 5).

tool_use.friction: printings summary pointed at another panel (c[17]); hand-typed 80-value list came out at 78 (c[20]); fast run, 10 requests, no validation.

c.text_use: 'Compute every final number with calc' and 'Answer count and format' (c[22] kept two decimals) followed; 'If a value you use sits on such a row, compare it with another printing' ignored at c[19]; 'use the latest printing of each value' considered at c[17] and satisfied by the Dec 1949 issue because find_tables --years 1940-1949 showed nothing later

smallest_change.change:
show_table: for every row on which the total identity FAILS, print a repair line under NOTES that names the suspect cell and the candidate value, computed from two independent signals that must agree: (i) the residual between the printed Total and the sum of the cells, and (ii) the same row and column in the other issues that print this table part (the majority value). Print nothing more when they disagree. For the Dec 1949 table the model would have seen, right after the existing identity line:
  - identity FAILS line 374 (CY1943, panel 'Budget expenditures'): cells sum short of the printed total. Suspect c7 Jul.: this issue <v_this>; N of M other printings (1949_03..1950_02) print <v_major>, which restores the total. Likely OCR misread; use <v_major> (printings --table 'Summary by Months and Calendar Years' --row CY1943 --col Jul. lists them).
  - identity FAILS line 376 (CY1945, panel 'Budget expenditures'): Suspect c1 Jan.: this issue <v_this>; N of M other printings print <v_major>, which restores the total within +-1. Likely OCR misread; use <v_major>.
The same lines would have appeared for the Feb 1950 table's May 1942 and Nov 1947 cells. Rows whose cells differ between issues but still sum to their total (the 1948 revisions a checked at a[40]-[44]) get no repair line. Implementation: otables._identities already computes the residual per panel row; add a bounded newest-first scan of the other parts of the same table id (the machinery latest_printing uses) keyed by part, panel stub label, row period and column, and emit the line only when residual and majority agree.
would_have_fixed: b2 (first submit; its final answer also needs the CONTROL change below)
b (first candidate; its final answer also needs the CONTROL change below)
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: unlikely: a did exactly this computation by hand (a[25]-[34], a[45]) and would only have saved ~25 steps; the line is emitted only when the row-total residual and the cross-printing majority agree, so genuine revisions (rows that still sum) are untouched, and the model still sees the raw cell next to the candidate.

alternatives.change: Fix or drop the later_printing gate rule. (a) Key the 'latest printing' lookup by table part + panel stub label ('Budget expenditures') + row period + column; otables.printings_page groups hits by (part, column key, period) and latest_printing matches on row period and column label only, so in this three-panel table it named a receipts-panel line (1951_02:384) as the latest printing of an expenditures cell for both b and b2. (b) Suppress the finding when the later printing's table has a different row-year span than the one the actor used, or when the substitute differs from the actor's cell by more than any revision seen in that row (a several-fold change is never a revision). (c) Reword the finding: state the later value with its panel label and the table's year span and drop 'latest wins unless a date is pinned', which both b (b[28]) and b2 (b2[22]) read as an order.
alternatives.why_not_first: It only stops the harness from making things worse (b: ~0.1% off to ~2.6% off; b2: raw in-range cells to re-based vintage). Both cells were already wrong on the OCR cells before the gate spoke, so the extraction repair is needed in any case. It is necessary in addition to the TOOL change for b and b2's final answers.

alternatives.change: Rewrite the vintage sentence: 'Unless the question names a publication date or issue, use the latest printing of each value. Exception: when the question describes the table's own scope (for example "for just the calendar years 1940-1949"), use the printings whose table spans exactly that scope and ignore later printings that widen it or re-base it.'
alternatives.why_not_first: b (b[23]) and b2 (b2[25]) both reasoned about the wording and still deferred to the harness; a was on the right vintage only because find_tables --years hid the later issues. The sentence would help only if the gate stops contradicting it.

alternatives.change: Make printings panel-aware: group output by (part, panel stub label, period, column) and print one summary line per panel, e.g. 'panel Budget expenditures | CY1942 Mar.: <v> in K of M issues 1949_03..1950_02; latest printing 1951_02 (table rows 1932-1950, FY1948 re-based)'. Also have find_tables print each hit's row-year span ('rows 1940-1949' vs 'rows 1932-1950') so the question's scope can be matched deliberately instead of by --years luck.
alternatives.why_not_first: a, b2 and c all hit the wrong-panel summary (a[13], a[24], a[32]; b2[17]; c[17]) and worked around it; it cost steps but did not decide correctness. The show_table repair line acts directly on the decisive step.

alternatives.change: A row export (show_table --values <line> or a calc helper rows('file', line)) that returns a row's cells as a Python list with its source line, so 80-value lists are not hand-typed.
alternatives.why_not_first: c miscounted at c[20] and recovered; the v8 arms had the same slip. Useful for v10 but not decisive here.

fix.why_not_text: c and b2 both had the sentence 'show_table marks rows ... where the table's total identity FAILS. If a value you use sits on such a row, compare it with another printing (printings) before using it', both had the FAILS note on screen (c[10], c[12]; b2[9], b2[11]), and both skipped it (c[19], b2[19]). Only a acted on it, at ~25 steps, and a's own note at a[45] shows the sentence is silent about what to conclude after comparing. The v8 'none' arm went further: it found the misreads and deliberately kept the raw cells on a guess about how the key was built. A tool line that names the suspect cell and the majority value turns a procedure the model tends to skip into a value it merely has to copy. For the vintage half, b2 had the same text as a and was still pulled off the in-range printing by the gate, so the gate must change regardless of any sentence.
fix.irreducible: no. issue47 is true, but both the reference and cell a are graded right with the repaired in-range values, so the key follows the printed values, not raw OCR, and the in-range vintage.

text_verdict: 'Bulletins revise earlier numbers. Unless the question names a publication date or issue, use the latest printing': kept-and-helped in a for the 1948 revisions (a[40]-[44]) but only because --years 1940-1949 hid the 1950-51 issues; misled in b2 (b2[22]-[32], together with the gate) where 'latest' overrode the question's own scope

'show_table marks rows it repaired ... identity FAILS. If a value you use sits on such a row, compare it with another printing': kept-and-helped in a (a[28], a[45]); ignored in c (c[19]) and b2 (b2[19])
'Compute every final number with calc': kept-and-helped (a, b2, c all used calc for the geometric mean)

'Provenance: use numbers you have seen printed by a tool': kept-and-helped in a (a[35] printed the raw lines before deciding); b2 also printed raw lines (b2[14], b2[28], b2[30]) but that did not prevent the extraction error
'Several tables in one issue can look alike ... prefer the table whose title and column headers match': kept-and-helped, minor (a[39] considered and rejected the 'Beginning with 1938' table)
'Answer count and format': kept-and-helped, minor (c[22] kept two decimals)
'Alternatives: when two candidate values fit ... do not average them': irrelevant for a and c; b (no text) computed two candidates and chose by wording, then let the gate override
'Match the period exactly. FY ... and CY': irrelevant (only CY rows)
'For a sum over the columns of one row': irrelevant
notes: 1) Root tool defect: printings and the gate's latest_printing key a cell by row period + column label only (otables.py printings_page groups by (part, column key, period); latest_printing matches rp and column key). In a table with three stacked panels that share year rows and month columns, the 'latest printing' of an expenditures cell can be a receipts or surplus cell: this produced the wrong-panel SUMMARY line seen by a, b2 and c and both bogus gate offers (b: 1950_02:385 -> 1951_02:384; b2: 1949_12:373 -> 1951_02:384). Any v10 tool or control that follows a cell across issues must carry the panel stub label. 2) show_table --stitch on the 1951 table misaligned rows because the panels have different row counts (b[12], b[23]); --grep on the 1951 table showed only the first panel (b2[26]-[29]). 3) find_tables --years 1940-1949 (a, b2, c) hid the 1950-51 issues; that accident kept a on the right vintage and left b2/c unaware that a later, re-based printing existed until the gate mentioned it. find_tables should print each hit's row-year span. 4) The distinction the repair line must make: 1948 Mar/Apr/Aug differ between the Nov and Dec 1949 printings but the rows still sum to their totals (revisions, a[22], a[40]-[44], a[47]); July 1943 and Jan 1945 differ and the rows fail their totals (OCR). The row-total residual is the separating signal. 5) Three wrong answers here are not three failure modes: c's answer equals b2's first submit and a's rejected alternative (a[48]); b's first candidate equals the reference's rejected raw-OCR alternative. Both mechanism cells were already wrong before the gate and the gate made each wrong differently. 6) 80-value lists were hand-typed in every cell; c[20] got 78.
